request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for acute appendicitis with CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis confirming the diagnosis. Laparoscopic appendectomy was performed successfully. Peritoneal and nasopharyngeal fluid samples were obtained for culture. The patient was found to be COVID-19 positive via nasopharyngeal swab after surgery and was subsequently isolated with contact precautions. The peritoneal fluid tested negative for COVID-19. An elevated CRP level was noted, and he was placed on ampicillin-sulbactam for empiric antibiotic coverage. Despite progressing through his hospital stay, he continued to be intermittently febrile. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 4 when he was afebrile and asymptomatic to quarantine in his home for two weeks.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
Laparoscopic appendectomy, empiric antibiotic coverage with ampicillin-sulbactam

Complications:
COVID-19 positive status in nasopharyngeal fluid sample only, Streptococcus anginosus positive peritoneal fluid culture

Follow-up:
Patient to quarantine at home for two weeks post-discharge. Follow-up with primary care physician as necessary.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission was acute appendicitis, which was confirmed on CT and treated with laparoscopic appendectomy. The COVID-19 positive swab was found after surgery and is a secondary diagnosis, so it is not the principal diagnosis.

Acute appendicitis falls in ICD-10-AM Chapter XI (Diseases of the digestive system) under K35, "Acute appendicitis". The Streptococcus anginosus positive peritoneal culture suggests there may have been peritonitis or abscess, which would be coded at the 4th and 5th character level (K35.2, K35.3). The question asks only for the three-character category, so the answer is K35 either way.

CODE: K35
